UK guidelines2 only recommend such treatment as part of a clinical study. In patients with unresectable locally advanced disease (stage IIIB and unresectable IIIA), the use of platinum- based chemotherapy either before or with radiotherapy has resulted in a modest increase in survival according to the findings of a number of meta-analyses17,27-29 and has be- come recommended therapy.13,30 Regimens usually in- clude cisplatin plus either etoposide, a vinca alkaloid, or a taxane. The issue of dosage and sequencing has been in- vestigated;30,31 concurrent chemotherapy with radiothera- py (chemoradiotherapy) is considered by some to be supe- rior to sequential therapy,12,14,31,32 but others2 recommend sequential chemoradiotherapy or caution29 that the magni- tude of increased benefit with concurrent therapy is not yet clear. Chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery (trimodali- ty therapy) is also under investigation.30 Encouraging results32 suggest that this approach of chemotherapy, radi- ation, and surgery may improve progression-free survival when compared with chemotherapy and radiation alone. Chemotherapy may also be used for advanced metastatic disease (stage IV), which is detected in 40 to 50% of pa- tients at presentation, although response is poor with a 5- year survival rate of only about 1%. Meta-analyses have shown a modest improvement in survival and symptom control in patients given chemotherapy compared with those given best supportive care.17,33 Furthermore, combi- nation chemotherapy has improved responses compared with single drug therapy,34 particularly platinum-based combinations.35 When compared with combinations of newer drugs (including vinorelbine, gemcitabine, taxanes, and irinotecan), platinum-based regimens still have a high- er response, but they cause more toxicity and 1-year sur- vival is not significantly different.35 In general, cisplatin- based chemotherapy has become the standard of care for advanced disease,2,12-15,30 although no particular regimen has been identified as superior.36,37 Regimens include cis- platin or carboplatin combined with either gemcitabine, ir- inotecan, etoposide, vinblastine, vinorelbine, docetaxel, or paclitaxel.14,15 Older triple regimens
